text:
devon: Heads up — we've been getting repeated 504s for hosted inference tenant tg-42 since 09:12 UTC. Spike coincides with a burst of requests from the customer.
lucas: Seeing the same in SLO alerts. 5xx rate jumped from 0.3% to ~8% across gateway nodes.
maria: Any relation to recent routing changes?
devon: Not that I can see. Router logs show long upstream response times and 'no healthy upstream' in a few cases.
emily: Checked KEDA/HPA metrics. KEDA reported scaling trigger at ~09:11, but HPA only added pods after ~2m. Pod init times are ~90s due to model warmup + image pull.
aj: That delay would explain 504s. KEDA poll interval and HPA stabilization window might be misaligned.
lucas: Paste of the kube events/logs I grabbed:
```
Normal  ScalingReplicaSet  2m (x3 over 3m)  keda-scaledobject   Triggered scale to 10
Normal  SuccessfulCreate   1m                 replicaset-controller  Created pod inference-abc-xyz
Warning BackOff            1m                 kubelet                Back-off pulling image "registry/repo:latest"
Normal  Created            30s                kubelet                Started container model-server
Warning Unhealthy         20s                 kubelet                Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 500
```

maria: Readiness probe failure + long image pull is the culprit. But why did HPA wait? HPA settings show `stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300` and `behavior: scaleDown` config looks fine but scaleUp has `policies` with `periodSeconds: 60` and `stabilizationWindowSeconds` inherited.
emily: And KEDA is using Prometheus scaler with `pollingInterval: 30s` and `cooldownPeriod: 300s`. So KEDA triggers but HPA cooldown prevents aggressive add.
support: Customer reports every request during the burst got 504, they escalated to SEV. I told them we're investigating and prioritized a mitigation.
devon: Repro steps I used:
1) Run load test hitting /v1/generate with concurrency 40 to 60 for tenant tg-42.
2) Observe queue backlog at gateway and KEDA webhook firing.
3) Observe pods created but remaining NotReady for ~70-120s.

Commands:
```
kubectl get hpa -n prod inference-hpa -o yaml
kubectl get scaledobject -n prod inference-scaledobject -o yaml
kubectl describe pod inference-abc-xyz -n prod
```

lucas: Quick mitigation idea: temporarily set HPA minReplicas = 4 and reduce `stabilizationWindowSeconds` to 60, and lower KEDA `cooldownPeriod` to 60 for the scaledobject. Also add an initContainer to pull the model image into a warm cache — but that's a longer-term change.
aj: We pushed a short-lived rollback patch to reduce HPA stabilization to 60s and bumped minReplicas to 3 for the burst window. Deployed at 09:24 UTC.
oncall-bot: Incident 2026-04-05T09:24:30 UTC - mitigation applied: HPA minReplicas=3, stabilizationWindowSeconds=60 (rolled by @aj)
srebot: Observability update: 5xx rate dropped to 1.2% within 45s of change, error budget burn slowed.
maria: Can we reproduce the issue in staging with identical HPA/KEDA config? We should validate image pull time + readiness probe thresholds.
devon: I reproduced with a scaled-down tenant in staging; if model server init > 60s, gateway times out. Repro steps attached above.
emily: Root cause summary: combination of (a) long model init/image pull (70-120s), (b) KEDA trigger -> HPA race where HPA scaling behavior/stabilization prevented enough pods being marked Ready fast enough, (c) readiness probe failures during model warmup causing gateway to return 504s while queue backlogged.
lucas: Postmortem action items:
- Adjust HPA behavior to allow faster scaleUp during burst windows (runbook change).
- Add a pre-warm path: keep a pool of standby pods (minReplicas >= 3 for tenants with burst SLAs).
- Change readinessProbe to be more permissive during init (longer initialDelaySeconds or use a separate /healthz?warm handler).
- Optimize image delivery (use smaller runtime image + local mirror, or preload images on nodes).
- Tune KEDA pollingInterval/cooldown alignment with HPA.

support: I'll send the interim status to the customer: explanation, mitigation applied, ETA for full fix (ETA TBD after infra planning).
devon: Will follow up in <2 hours with reproducibility report and proposed runbook changes.
maria: Assigning action owners: lucas -> HPA runbook, emily -> scaledobject/KEDA tuning, aj -> short-term infra tweaks, devon -> repro validation and docs.

emily: One more note: We found a misconfigured annotation on the deployment: `autoscaling.alpha.kubernetes.io/behavior: none` on a previous canary made HPA ignore keda recommendations for ~12h. We'll scrub annotations across prod.
lucas: Thanks team. Logging the incident for a full postmortem. If anyone finds additional logs add them here. :thumbsup:
